column13: And that is: “in absolute truth it was all for the sake of Israel — only that they did not intend it so.” And therefore “all the letters of words of Torah that were in them” — from Hashem’s outpouring [upon them] in Creation — “were taken from them and given to Israel,” “the inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov” (Devarim 33:4) — and [therefore] “a gentile who engages in the Torah is liable to death” (Sanhedrin 59a)] of the congregation of Yaakov’ — an inheritance for us, and not for them.”.

column15: Concerning the evening prayer (Ma’ariv), which is optional (reshut), and the afternoon prayer (Minchah): during the daytime of clarity, a person serves God through fixed halakhic boundaries, whereas at night—when darkness and concealment surround a person—he draws down new illumination even into places that appear optional or outside explicit obligation, discovering the will of Heaven within the hiddenness of the night.
